This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Two-feel**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Bass lines](index.qmd#bass)

## The pattern

Half notes on beats 1 and 3, root then fifth, with an occasional pickup into the next bar. The lighter feel a band often plays on the head before the bass starts to walk.

It belongs in *Swing*, *Jazz ballad* and *Stride piano*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Two-feel","opts":{"bassFeel":"two"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Roots on 1 and 3

Start with something simpler. The root on beats 1 and 3, held; one note a bar in 3/4. A chord that changes in between gets its root when it arrives.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass-halves.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Two-feel, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Half notes on 1 and 3, root then fifth, with a swung pickup into the next bar now and then. Let each note ring for its full two beats: the line breathes in two while the drummer plays in four.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Two-feel","opts":{"bassFeel":"two"}},{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3 (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 120 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Two-feel","opts":{"bassFeel":"two"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7 G7|Em7 A7|Dm7 G7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Two-feel","opts":{"bassFeel":"two"}}]'></div>

## In other styles

The same bass line in other styles it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

## How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Roots on 1 and 3](bass-halves.qmd).
- **Leads to:** [12/8 ballad](bass-twelve8.qmd), [Walking](bass-walk.qmd), [So What: the bass call](bass-sowhat.qmd), [Killer Joe: two-bar vamp](bass-killerjoe.qmd): the patterns that use this one as a step.
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [Stride](chords-stride.qmd) (comping rhythm), [Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah](chords-oompah.qmd) (comping rhythm), [Root and fifth](bass-alt.qmd) (bass line).
- **Plays with, in swing:** [Varied](chords-auto.qmd) (comping rhythm), [Jazz time](drums-auto.qmd) (drum groove).
- **Other bass lines in the Jazz group:** [Walking](bass-walk.qmd), [Chord tones (learning to walk)](bass-arp.qmd), [Boogaloo riff](bass-riff.qmd), [Boogie-woogie](bass-boogie.qmd), [Boogie-woogie octaves](bass-boogie-oct.qmd), [Yancey figure](bass-yancey.qmd), [Boogaloo riff, walking at times](bass-riffwalk.qmd).
